title: Selling with Double Meanings
text:
Advertisers have long relied on double meanings, since a phrase that signals two things at once can slip past a viewer's guard. A slogan that seems to praise a product while quietly suggesting something else may be remembered far longer than a plain claim. The pleasure lies in the moment of recognition, when the audience discovers the second sense for itself.

Critics, however, note that such ambiguity can mislead as easily as it charms. When the hidden meaning is an insinuation rather than a joke, the consumer may accept a claim that would be rejected if stated openly. The ethical question is therefore not whether wordplay is clever, but whether it respects the intelligence of the people it addresses.

questions.text: According to paragraph one, what can a slogan with two meanings do?
options: Be forgotten faster than a plain claim
Be remembered far longer than a plain claim

questions.text: According to paragraph two, what might a consumer accept when the hidden meaning is an insinuation?
options: A claim that would be rejected if stated openly
A price increase for no reason

questions.text: What does the passage suggest about the pleasure of wordplay in advertising?
options: It depends on the audience discovering the second sense for itself
It comes from repeating the same phrase
It is found only in printed catalogues
It disappears once the meaning is known

questions.text: What central ethical question does the passage raise?
options: Whether wordplay is expensive to produce
Whether wordplay respects the intelligence of its audience
Whether advertisers should stop using adjectives

vocabulary.translation: a short, memorable phrase used in advertising
vocabulary.definition: a brief catchy phrase used to promote a product

vocabulary.translation: a hint of something unpleasant, suggested indirectly
vocabulary.definition: an indirect suggestion of something negative

vocabulary.translation: the quality of having more than one possible meaning
vocabulary.definition: uncertainty caused by words that can be read in different ways

vocabulary.translation: the moment of identifying something familiar
vocabulary.definition: the act of realising what something is or means
